name: Nullframe GhostTouch Infiltration Glove
description:
Skintight wrist-length gloves in charcoal-grey synthetic dermis, nearly indistinguishable from bare skin at distance. The outer surface is micro-textured with passive print-disruption coating — contact leaves no usable fingerprint, only smeared static. Inner palm channels are seeded with gecko-fiber adhesion strips that activate under pressure, releasing cleanly on flex.

Cutaway options exist for augmented index and middle fingers — pre-slit seams that can be popped open without degrading the glove's integrity. Street label, no branding visible. Bought in matched pairs sealed in unmarked pouches.
functionality: Print-masking on all contact surfaces. Gecko-grip activates at 40%+ palm compression — effective on glass, polymer panels, and wet metal. Aug-compatible cutaway finger seams for chrome digits. Thin enough for full haptic sensitivity on touchpads and BCI panels.
what_it_says: You move through places you were not invited, and you leave nothing behind.
story_hooks: A pair surfaces at a Tier 5 Spire burglary scene — the gecko-fiber signature matches a batch sold exclusively through a Circuit black market broker who claims they were stolen from their own stock.
The print-disruption coating has begun failing on a specific production run, and whoever sold them knows — but hasn't issued a recall.
A Tier 3 accountant is found wearing a pair during a routine office audit; they have no explanation for how they got them.
